title: On-call & Incident Response Playbook
author: Avery Chen
content:
Overview

This document is the canonical On-call & Incident Response Playbook for Redwood Inference. It codifies our incident lifecycle, severity definitions, on-call rotations and responsibilities, runbook templates, postmortem process, game day guidance, and status page / customer communications templates. The goal is to ensure consistent, measurable responses that minimize customer impact and accelerate safe, verifiable remediation.

Principles
- Safety first: protect customer data and avoid actions that could worsen impact.
- Fast detection, measured response: prioritize rapid acknowledgement and containment, then durable fixes.
- Blameless postmortems: focus on systems and process improvements.
- Continuous improvement: run regular game days and triage follow-ups.

Key SLOs & Alerting Thresholds
(Used to drive paging and prioritization)
| SLO / Metric | Target | Page threshold | Notes |
|---|---:|---:|---|
| API availability (hosted inference) | 99.95% monthly | outage if < 99.5% in 15m window | Pager for widespread customer impact |
| Request error rate (5xx) | < 0.5% p95 | Pager if > 3% sustained for 5m or p95 error increase >3x baseline | Alert for degraded service |
| Latency (generation token p95) | < 800ms | Alert if p95 > 2s for 10m | Impact to UX |
| Queue depth / backlog on worker pool | N/A | Pager if queue > 2x normal for 5m | Indicates capacity pressure |
| Model regression (semantic quality) | N/A | Pager if automated eval failure rate increases by >5% for 30m | Triage as high-priority product incident |

Severity matrix
- Sev 1 (P1): Complete outage or critical data loss. Requires immediate paging and war room.
- Sev 2 (P2): Major degradation affecting many customers or major feature (e.g., generation returns 50% errors). Requires on-call engagement within 15 minutes.
- Sev 3 (P3): Partial degradation, single-customer impact, or internal tooling down. On-call should acknowledge within 1 hour.
- Sev 4 (P4): Non-urgent issues, maintenance, or minor bugs; tracked in backlog.

Escalation & Paging policy
1. Pager triggers: PagerDuty alerts route to primary on-call for the relevant service/team. Alerts must contain: summary, severity, affected services, initial diagnostic links (logs/metrics/dumps).
2. Primary on-call: ack within 5 minutes for P1, 15 minutes for P2. If unable to make progress after 15 minutes (P1) / 30 minutes (P2), escalate to secondary.
3. Secondary on-call: take ownership if primary is unavailable or request escalation.
4. Engineering manager: contacted for P1 within 30 minutes and for P2 if escalation criteria met.
5. Incident Commander (IC): Appointed for all P1 incidents and high-impact P2 incidents. IC responsibilities outlined below.

On-call rotations & responsibilities
- Rotation model: 1-week rotations for primary and secondary across SRE and service teams. On-call schedule is maintained in the on-call calendar and PagerDuty.
- Responsibilities of the primary on-call:
  - Triage and acknowledge alerts.
  - Run relevant runbooks to attempt containment/mitigation.
  - Communicate status to stakeholders and update the incident channel.
  - If required, appoint an IC and set a war room (Slack huddle or Zoom).
- Responsibilities of the secondary on-call:
  - Provide follow-up support and relieve primary if they need to off-ramp.
  - Own escalations to product/manager level if remediation needs coordination.
- Handover: Each on-call must post a brief handover note at the start and end of shift summarizing active incidents, mitigations in place, and follow-ups.

Incident lifecycle (step-by-step)
1. Detect & Alert
   - Alert fires and creates a PagerDuty incident. PagerDuty should include runbook links, recent error spikes link, and Grafana dashboard.
2. Acknowledge & Triage
   - Primary on-call ack the alert and classify severity.
   - Capture initial facts: time, symptoms, scope (customers affected), and hypothesis.
3. Contain / Mitigate
   - Execute the service runbook for the symptom. Typical actions: restart workers, scale up pool, toggle circuit breaker (feature flag), or failover to backup model variant.
   - Record actions and timestamps in the incident timeline.
4. Escalate & Coordinate
   - If not resolved within defined window escalate to secondary then manager, and appoint IC for P1.
   - IC sets communication cadence (every 15m for P1 until stable).
5. Restore & Validate
   - Restore full service and validate against health checks and synthetic traffic.
   - Keep the incident open for at least one verification period (30–60m) to ensure stability.
6. Communicate & Close
   - Post customer-facing status updates (see templates below) and internal incident summary.
   - After close, assign postmortem owner and follow postmortem cadence.

Runbook templates (canonical)
- Each service must have a short runbook with: symptoms, quick checks, mitigation steps, escalation path, rollback steps, and verification. Keep runbooks to one page where possible.

Example: Hosted API - 5xx spike runbook
1. Symptoms:
   - Sudden increase in 5xx errors observed on API-prod-targets, p95 error rate >3% for 5m.
2. Quick checks:
   - Check Grafana: request rate, CPU/GPU utilization, worker queue depth.
   - Check logs for recent deploys (last 30m).
3. Mitigations (in order):
   - If new deploy in last 30m: roll back the deployment to previous stable tag.
   - If worker pool exhausted: scale up Dedicated pools or trigger autoscaler.
   - If model OOMs on worker: switch routing policy to smaller model variant.
4. Escalation:
   - If mitigations do not reduce 5xx by 50% in 15m escalate to secondary/IC.
5. Verification:
   - Confirm p95 error rate returns to baseline and synthetic canaries succeed.

Postmortem process and template
- Owner: IC or individual assigned within 48 hours of incident close.
- Timeline: Draft due within 3 business days; review within 7 days; publish within 10 business days.
- Tone: blameless, factual, and focused on remediation.
- Minimum sections (each a top-level heading in the postmortem):
  - Summary: one-paragraph impact and timeline.
  - Detection & Timeline: bullet timeline of events with timestamps.
  - Root Cause: concise technical cause and contributing factors.
  - Impact: customers affected, duration, SLAs breached.
  - Remediation & Mitigation: short-term fixes applied during the incident.
  - Action Items: owner, due date, verification steps.
  - Follow-ups: game day or infra changes required.

Postmortem checklist
- [ ] Incident assigned an owner within 48 hours
- [ ] Draft posted to Confluence and linked to incident ticket
- [ ] Blameless review completed with involved teams
- [ ] Action items tracked and added to team roadmap or backlog

Game days & testing
- Cadence: each team runs at least one game day per quarter. SRE runs company-wide major game day twice per year (failover, upgrades, scale).
- Scenarios: capacity surge, region outage, model regression, KMS/HSM failure, data-residency rollback.
- Outcomes: validate runbooks, measure MTTR, and identify automation opportunities.

Status page & customer communications templates
- Purpose: provide timely, clear, and consistent updates to customers. Use the status page for public broadcast and personalized communications for impacted enterprise customers via CSMs.

Template: Initial acknowledgement (short)
Subject: "[Redwood] Incident detected affecting inference API"
Body:
We are aware of an issue affecting the Redwood Inference API and are investigating.
What we know: {brief summary, e.g., increased 5xx errors for text generation} 
What we're doing: {short list, e.g., triaging, rolling back recent deploy, scaling workers} 
Next update: within 15 minutes or when we have a new development.

Template: Customer update (progress)
Subject: "[Redwood] Update: Incident affecting inference API"
Body:
Current status: {eg, mitigations applied and partial recovery observed} 
Impact: {customers/regions/features affected} 
Next steps: {what we will do next} 
ETA for next update: {timebox} 

Template: Resolution
Subject: "[Redwood] Incident resolved - inference API"
Body:
Status: Resolved. Service is operating normally and health checks show stable results.
Summary of impact: {duration, customers affected, and root cause summary} 
Follow-up: A postmortem will be published at {link} within 10 business days.

Internal escalation / press guidance
- For any potential press or regulatory impact, contact Legal and Communications immediately and mark the incident as "restricted".

Ownership, tools, and links
- Primary tools: PagerDuty, Slack (#incidents), Grafana, Honeycomb, Sentry, internal deployment dashboard.
- On-call schedule: maintain in PagerDuty and sync to the on-call calendar.
- Runbooks: link to service-specific runbooks stored under /confluence/oncall-and-incident-response/runbooks (team-runbooks).

RACI (summary)
- Responsible: Primary on-call (first responder), Secondary on-call (support), IC (coordination for P1).
- Accountable: Engineering manager for service.
- Consulted: Product, Security, Legal (if data exposure).
- Informed: Customer Success, Execs for major incidents.

Revision history
- 2025-09-15: created (Avery Chen)
- 2025-12-06: updated thresholds and runbook links (reviewers: Marcus Patel, Lina Gomez)
- 2026-02-20: clarified escalation windows and added model regression paging (Avery Chen)

Appendix: quick command snippets
- Roll back last deploy (kubectl example):
  - kubectl rollout undo deployment/inference-service -n prod --to-revision=<REVISION>
- Restart worker pod (k8s):
  - kubectl delete pod <pod-name> -n prod
- Trigger autoscaler (CLI):
  - infra-cli scale pool inference-prod --size <N>

If you have questions or need a runbook created for a new service, contact the SRE leads or open an RFC in /confluence/eng-platform/roadmap.
